dedupe_keys.name: eqmt aegean earthquake magnitude and occurrence time model

description: The EQMT authors publish Python code for an exploratory fault-aware earthquake forecasting model. The public GitHub repository has model modules, magnitude and time notebooks, batch runners and a GPL-3.0 licence. The paper describes mapping fault traces into a graph, deriving node embeddings, combining recent seismic-event features, then using attention-based sequence models for magnitude and CatBoost for occurrence-time classification. It reports evaluation on northern Aegean events from 2004 to 2024. The repository is free to view, but the inspected root did not establish independently reusable trained weights or a complete event-and-fault input dataset. This code may support experimental earthquake-hazard scenario generation for roads, ports and power networks; it must not be treated as an operational warning system or a calibrated probability model for another region. A limited regional test and uncertain transfer to other fault settings are major caveats. The model can be paired with data-era5-reanalysis only for separate weather exposure in compound-hazard studies, not as a required EQMT input. No code was downloaded or run.
inputs: Mapped fault traces and graph features
name: EQMT Aegean earthquake magnitude and occurrence-time model
notes: G3 G3-0603. Draft only. No resource files downloaded or software executed. Article data statement said code would become public after acceptance; the public GitHub repository now contains code. Trained weights and full input dataset were not established from the inspected root.
